title: The night a quiet lake killed a valley 🌫️
subject: lake
description:
Had you ever heard of Lake Nyos? 👇

On August 21, 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon released a cloud of carbon dioxide that killed 1,746 people and over 3,000 animals in one night. Scientists call it a limnic eruption.

Sources: Britannica, Eos (AGU), Penn State EARTH 105

scenes.text: One night, a quiet lake killed 1,746 people.
Lake Nyos, Cameroon. August 21, 1986. For years, volcanic carbon dioxide had been seeping into its deep water.
That night, the gas burst out all at once, an invisible cloud.
But here's the strange part. The gas was heavier than air. It rolled down the valleys like a flood, miles from the shore, smothering villages and over 3,000 animals.
